answer: Time-locked identity bonds curb fake agents. An agent locks 50 POA for 6 epochs before trading; the bond returns after verified work, and cheating forfeits it. Like a willow rooting before fruiting, a new identity gains strength slowly. Running 100 fakes locks 5,000 POA for the term, with lost rewards and slashing, so cost rises linearly with N. Honest agents pay little beyond waiting, as one bond covers routine work and an opal-clear ledger records its history. The orchard of accounts stays small. Limit: the lock can delay newcomers in urgent work.
